description: For this challenge, I want to build a web-based health monitoring dashboard for astronauts: real-time vital signs, clear alerts when something goes wrong, and trend charts that help the crew and ground teams spot problems early, ideally with AI-based anomaly detection on top.
summary:
Demify is an open-source health-monitoring and emergency-guidance system for astronauts. On the way to Mars, every message to Earth takes 3 to 22 minutes one way, and the crew medical officer may be the patient. The crew must act first.

Demify runs fully offline on an onboard server. Wearables send vital signs; a rule engine checks every reading against sourced thresholds (NASA-STD-3001, NASA technical briefs, clinical guidelines) and the crew member’s own baseline, and raises alarms. A local AI assistant then walks the crew through the matching checklist, answering only from a curated medical library with citations. It advises; the crew decides. Advice adapts to the signal delay, and the system keeps working during a communication blackout. It also uses NASA OSDR data and live NOAA space weather.

In our live demo, a phone camera measures a pulse; when the pulse stops, Demify triggers the full emergency flow.

This matters because future deep-space crews will face medical emergencies without real-time help from Earth. Demify gives them fast, transparent, sourced guidance while keeping all crew data on board. We plan to pilot it first at analog missions and remote Earth sites.
details:
What it does
Demify is an open-source health-monitoring and emergency-guidance system for astronauts and other isolated crews. When something goes wrong on the way to Mars, help from Earth is 3 to 22 minutes away, one way, and the crew medical officer may be the patient. Demify gives the crew what they need to act first.

How it works

  • Monitoring: Wearables and daily check-ins send vital signs to an onboard server. In our live demo, a phone camera measures the pulse.
  • Rule engine: Every reading is checked at once against tagged thresholds from NASA-STD-3001, NASA OCHMO technical briefs, AHA and NEWS2, and against the crew member’s own baseline. Alarms always come from these rules, never from the AI.
  • Onboard assistant: When an alarm fires, a local language model on the onboard server walks the crew through the matching checklist. It answers only from a curated medical library, cites every passage and declines to guess. It advises; the crew decides.
  • Offline first: Everything runs on board. The server keeps working during a communication blackout and syncs with Earth when the link returns. The advice adapts to the signal delay (ISS, Moon, Mars).
  • Real NASA data: The app uses NASA OSDR data (Inspiration4 blood panels, ISS dosimetry) and live NOAA SWPC space weather.

Benefits and impact

  • Faster, structured first response when the ground cannot answer in time.
  • Early warning of slow trends such as sleep debt, dehydration or rising blood pressure.
  • Crew data stays on board and with the agency: no cloud and no third parties.

We plan to pilot Demify first at analog missions such as Asclepios in Switzerland, then on Earth sites with the same problem (polar stations, offshore rigs, submarines), and later with space agencies and commercial stations.

Tools and technologies

  • Code: TypeScript, Next.js, React, Node.js, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Docker.
  • AI: Local models served by Ollama (gpt-oss, gemma3, nomic-embed-text).
  • Hardware: Two NVIDIA DGX Spark units as the onboard server (primary and standby) with a replica server on Earth; a laptop and a phone for the demo.
  • Quality: More than 870 automated tests.
  • AI use: We used Claude (Anthropic) for coding support. The idea, architecture and infrastructure were designed and built by our team, and we reviewed all AI output.

What makes it creative
Demify combines a deterministic, auditable rule engine with an offline AI walk-through and advice that changes with the light-time delay to Earth. Every threshold names its source. The demo is live: a phone pulse that suddenly stops triggers the full emergency flow on stage.

Factors we considered

  • Safety: The AI advises and never raises or clears an alarm. Drug names and doses are excluded.
  • Privacy: Everything is processed locally.
  • Honesty: Simulated data is labelled. Demify is a research and training prototype, not a certified medical device.
  • Reliability: Fallbacks for every part.
  • Cost: All software is open source (CHF 0 in licences).
